title: Introduce KV-prefetch circuit breaker and adaptive token emission to stop TTFT spikes
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported sudden TTFT spikes and tokens/sec collapse when the model-serving prefetch stage issues concurrent KV cache warms. Root cause hypothesis: an unbounded prefetch loop plus aggressive token emission that creates transient worker saturation and kernel thrashing. This ticket implements a fast hotpatch: a circuit breaker around KV-prefetch, an adaptive token emission limiter, and a controlled canary rollout to private/dedicated tenants before wide release.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Replay customer trace from 2026-02-28 incident (trace id: trace-20260228-7f2c).
2) Run stress script with mix of short-chat and long-context requests (scripts/perf/kv_prefetch_stress.py).
3) Observe TTFT spike within 30s and tokens/sec drop on worker group gpu-rt-12.

Observed impact:
- TTFT increases 3x for first-token on multiplexed streams.
- Overall tokens/sec drops 40% for affected model variants.
- Customers A and B reported timeouts and raised severity P1/P0 support tickets.

Proposed fix:
- Add a circuit breaker guarding KV-prefetch requests per-worker with metrics: prefetch_inflight, prefetch_failures. When inflight > 12 or failure_rate > 10% over 60s, short-circuit prefetch and fall back to on-demand fetch.
- Implement adaptive token emission limiter (token_emission_rate) that scales down micro-bursts when router queue depth or kernel latency exceeds thresholds.
- Expose per-tenant override flags so enterprise Dedicated customers can opt out during testing.
- Add telemetry: prefetch_shortcircuits, emission_throttles, per-model tokens/sec, and first-byte latency by region.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature flag guarded change behind ff:kv_prefetch_cb and ff:adaptive_emission.
2) Deploy to staging and run perf regression suite (perf-suite/kv_prefetch.yaml).
3) Canary to 5% of traffic for Hosted and to a single Dedicated customer (Customer B) for 2 hours. Monitor first-byte latency and tokens/sec.
4) If stable, promote to 25% then 100% over 6h with automated rollback if TTFT increases >5% above baseline.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for circuit breaker state transitions and metrics emission.
- Integration test simulating prefetch failures to ensure fallback path is exercised.
- Load test with same model mix as customer traces.
- Include chaos test that randomly injects delayed KV responses to validate fallback behavior.

Notes: This is time-sensitive because affected customers have production traffic and SLA exposure. Aim for hotfix release runtime-2.4.1-hotfix with a coordinated postmortem within 72h of successful deploy.
